payload.finding: t0036 did not improve the prior champion: val_bpb=0.977341, delta=+0.004243. Hypothesis: The output softcap may be limiting the metric directly rather than only stabilising training. The head computes logits, casts to float32, then applies 15*tanh(logits/15), which asymptotically bounds every logit to plus or minus 15 and, more importantly, compresses differences once magnitudes approach that scale. val_bpb is a cross-entropy quantity, so it is exactly the size of the gap between the correct logit and its competitors that sets the achievable loss on confident predictions, and a model at 0.973 bpb makes many highly confident predictions on a small 8192-token vocabulary. payload.finding: t0046 did not improve the prior champion: val_bpb=0.972982, delta=+0.000278. Hypothesis: Gating is the one control-path addition that has paid in this campaign, and attention output has none. The value-embedding path is gated per head by 2*sigmoid of a linear map on 128 residual channels, and widening exactly that gate from 32 to 128 channels produced the only champion improvement in twenty nodes. Attention output receives no such treatment: every head contributes to the residual stream with a fixed unit weight regardless of context, so a head that is uninformative for a given token cannot be attenuated except through c_proj, which is a fixed linear map shared across all positions. Hypothesis: Averaging the endpoint of the trajectory paid 0.001103 in t0096, and the natural question is whether averaging the trajectory itself pays too. payload.finding: t0351 did not improve the prior champion: val_bpb=0.968349, delta=+0.001063. Hypothesis: Squared ReLU is unbounded above and is the only unbounded quantity left in the forward pass. Every other place where magnitude could run away has been given a ceiling and each one mattered: q and k are RMS-normalised per head, the residual stream is normalised before every block, and the output logits are softcapped at 13, an axis so steep that 7 cost 0.005206 and 30 cost 0.004637 around the optimum. The MLP activation has no such bound, and squaring makes its tail quadratic, so a single large pre-activation dominates the row that feeds c_proj. t0095 showed the shape of this nonlinearity is load-bearing, since replacing it with GELU cost 0.012431, which means the campaign should bound it rather than replace it. Clamping the squared activation at 64, roughly the value an input of 8 produces against a normalised stream whose elements are order one, should suppress that tail without touching the ordinary operating range.

payload.finding: t0353 improved the prior champion: val_bpb=0.966202, delta=-0.001084. Hypothesis: Every head in this champion must spend its full attention mass somewhere, because softmax normalises to one no matter what the window contains. That constraint bites hardest here: the SSL pattern gives two of every three layers a 256 token span, so most heads look at a short window that frequently holds nothing worth retrieving, and they are still forced to emit a convex combination of whatever is inside it. An attention sink is the usual escape, letting mass drain to a null slot, but this FA3 build exposes no sink argument and returns the softmax lse only as a non-differentiable auxiliary, so reconstructing a sink from the lse would silently produce wrong gradients rather than an error. The same escape is available downstream of the kernel: a per-head multiplicative gate on the attention output lets a head damp its own contribution toward zero when its window is uninformative, which is what draining mass to a sink accomplishes. If the forced-mass constraint is really costing this model, the gate should pay; if heads always have something useful inside a 256 token window, it should be neutral.

proposal.change_summary: One mechanism added to champion t0096. CausalSelfAttention gains attn_gate, an nn.Linear from the first 128 channels of x to n_head with no bias, constructed exactly like the existing ve_gate beside it. In forward, immediately before the heads are flattened for c_proj, the head-shaped attention output is multiplied by 2*sigmoid(attn_gate(x[..., :128])).unsqueeze(-1), the same 2*sigmoid form the value-embedding gate already uses, so the gate sits near one at initialisation and the change starts as near-identity. Placing it before the flatten covers the varlen and dense branches with a single edit. The new weight lives inside transformer.h, so setup_optimizer collects it into matrix_params, the parameter-count assertion still balances, and its (n_head, 128) shape joins the Muon shape-group that ve_gate already occupies. Nothing else moves: depth 12, SSL with a 256 short span, document masking, squared ReLU left unbounded after t0351 and t0352, softcap 13, EMA at 0.7 and 0.99.

A decrease would say the forced-mass constraint is real and short-window heads want an escape; a null at unchanged step count would say heads reliably find something useful inside 256 tokens and the constraint was not binding.

payload.finding: t0354 did not improve the prior champion: val_bpb=0.968982, delta=+0.002780. Hypothesis: t0353 gave every attention head an input-dependent gate on its own output and improved the champion by 0.001084, and it did so while losing throughput: steps fell from 2869 to about 2778, so the quality gain per step is larger than the net number shows. The stated reason was that softmax forces a head to spend its full attention mass even when its 256 token window holds nothing useful, and the gate is the escape. But that explanation is specific to attention, and there is a competing one that is not: sublayers in general benefit from being able to withdraw on tokens they have nothing to contribute to, and the residual stream benefits from not being written to. Those two explanations make different predictions about the MLP, which has no softmax and no forced-mass constraint at all. If gating the MLP branch also pays, the t0353 result was about sublayer withdrawal and the attention framing was incidental. If it is neutral or harmful, the softmax constraint was the real mechanism and gating belongs only where mass is forced.

payload.finding: t0355 did not improve the prior champion: val_bpb=0.967520, delta=+0.001318. Hypothesis: A note on the stage first: t0096 is the direct parent of t0353, so t0353 already contains every mechanism t0096 has and a literal merge of the two would reproduce the champion source exactly. The honest synthesis is between the two independent lines that actually exist in this tree, the window-structure line of t0073 and t0076 that set the SSL pattern and the 256 token short span, and the gating line that t0353 opened. The recombination is to make the gate structure follow the window structure. Decomposing the two gate trials against the token law, at 0.063 bpb per e-fold of steps, sharpens why this is the right move: t0353 gained 0.003139 of mechanism and handed back 0.002055 as throughput tax, while t0354 lost 0.001021 of mechanism on top of its own tax. So the attention gate is worth about three times its net score, and the largest gain available is not a new mechanism but paying less for the one already found. payload.finding: t0363 did not improve the prior champion: val_bpb=0.967716, delta=+0.001514. Every layer therefore begins by applying a random per-head rescaling of its attention output, and part of a 300 second budget is spent undoing it. I claimed the opposite in the record of t0353, t0354 and t0358, describing the gate as near-identity at initialisation; that claim was design intent that I never checked against the code and then copied forward.

Muon decays cautiously, with mask = (g * params) >= 0 so decay applies only where it agrees with the direction the gradient is already moving the weight, and never fights the update. adamw_step_fused decays unconditionally with p.mul_(1 - lr*wd). When I set the table rate by matching MATRIX_LR times WEIGHT_DECAY I matched the nominal rate but not the mechanism, so the value embeddings have been decayed on every step while the matrices whose rate I copied are decayed only on the subset of steps where the signs agree. The effective decay was therefore roughly double what I believed I was copying, which is a coherent explanation for why 0.00238 already sat near the optimum and 0.00476 overshot badly at 0.968105. payload.finding: t0416 did not improve the prior champion: val_bpb=0.965256, delta=+0.003546. Hypothesis: Attention placement matters at constant attention budget. The model spends its attention through a periodic tile, WINDOW_PATTERN='SSL' over 12 layers, which puts a full-context layer at 2, 5, 8 and 11 and a 256-token local window everywhere else. Every trial on this axis so far has moved the AMOUNT of global attention -- the short span, the long span, the ratio -- and all three directions peaked, so the axis reads as closed. But amount and position are different questions and only the first has been asked. Because _compute_window_sizes indexes pattern[layer_idx % len(pattern)], a 12-character pattern makes the modulo tile the identity and gives exact per-layer control, and holding the count of long layers at 4 holds attention FLOPs and kernel work exactly fixed. This trial moves the four long layers from uniformly spread to contiguous at the top: SSSSSSSSLLLL. The bet is that the uniform tile is an unexamined default rather than a tuned choice, and that a network which builds local features first and integrates globally last uses the same budget better than one that interrupts local processing every third layer. It is the same 'shape is a free axis' bet that has now won four times on decay schedules, applied to the one remaining structure that is laid out uniformly by default.

payload.finding:
t0434 ended as timeout. Hypothesis: Every head in this model is fully position-sensitive: RoPE rotates all 128 head dimensions. Partial rotary rotates only the first half and passes the tail through untouched, so each head carries both position-sensitive and position-invariant channels rather than being forced to encode content through a rotating basis.

The reason to expect this to matter HERE specifically, rather than as a generic architecture preference, is what the last four trials established about this model's attention. Placement work showed the model depends on periodic global integration and cannot afford a long local-only run: clustering the full-context layers cost +0.0031 and dissolving them into uniform medium spans cost +0.0028. So the four full-context layers are doing content retrieval over 2048 tokens, and at that distance the rotary phase between query and key has wrapped many times at base 30000 -- rotation is close to noise for the long-range matches those layers exist to make. Position-invariant channels give exactly those layers a way to match on content alone, while the eight 256-token layers keep enough rotated channels for local order. That is a specific prediction about a specific structure, not a general preference.

It is also nearly free, and may be slightly cheaper than the current code: half as much elementwise multiply-add in the rotary, though the concatenations may cancel that.. Result: 13 layers, n_embd 512, 4 heads -- champion width and head count. Compile mode reverts to default since depth changes the graph. Dry-run verified both constants and the rounding arithmetic.
proposal.expected_val_bpb_effect:
Parameters rise by roughly the size of one block plus one value-embedding table, so per-step FLOPs rise ~8% for the matrices. There is also a side effect I want on the record: the window pattern 'SSL' tiled over 13 layers puts long-window layers at 2, 5, 8, 11 plus the forced last one at 12 -- FIVE long layers instead of four, so attention FLOPs rise ~20% rather than ~8%. That is part of what 'one more layer' means under this pattern, but it means the arm is not a pure +1 block either.
Net expectation: steps fall to roughly 2500-2600 against the champion's 2806, a token-law debit near +0.0050. The capacity credit is the residual. From t0459, capacity was worth -0.00036 per percent of parameters at the 640-width point; a linear transfer to ~+10% parameters here predicts about -0.0036 and therefore a small loss. But the whole point is that within-plateau depth has behaved differently from cross-plateau size, so I do not trust that transfer and the measurement is the reason to run it.
proposal.hypothesis:
Retry after a contention abort. The first attempt was killed by the throughput guard at step 267 for running at 18.1% MFU -- a co-tenant arrived on the device mid-run. Its logged config confirms the edit did exactly what it was designed to do: n_layer 13, n_head 4, n_embd 512, the champion's width and head count with one extra layer. Nothing about the hypothesis changed; a guard abort writes a failed record so the coordinate needs a fresh hash.

Worth recording that this abort also validated the guard's new instrument in the opposite direction from the last one. The run was at 8.09 steps/s -- ABOVE the old 8.0 step-rate floor -- so the previous guard would have let a badly contaminated run finish and be scored. MFU catches fast-enough-but-starved runs as well as allowing slow-but-efficient ones.

The depth axis was never tested. It was tested as a model-SIZE axis, and nobody noticed -- including me, until t0459.

model_dim is derived from depth: ceil(depth * ASPECT_RATIO / HEAD_DIM) * HEAD_DIM. At the champion's ASPECT_RATIO 42 that gives:
    depth  8 -> width 384, 3 heads
    depth 10 -> width 512, 4 heads
    depth 11 -> width 512, 4 heads
    depth 12 -> width 512, 4 heads   <- champion
    depth 13 -> width 640, 5 heads
So the early exploration of 8/10/11/12/13/14 compared models of three different widths. Depth 12 won because it is the LARGEST depth that still rounds to 512 -- the champion sits at the top of a width plateau by an accident of integer rounding, not because 12 layers was measured against 13 layers. t0459 confirmed the cost of crossing the plateau: depth 13 at aspect 42 is 142.6M parameters against 96.5M, its steps fell 33.9%, and although it gained -0.017064 of capacity -- six times the MLP 5x arm -- it paid +0.024253 in throughput and lost.

Pairing depth 13 with ASPECT_RATIO 39 gives 13*39 = 507, which rounds to 512 with 4 heads: the champion's exact width and head count, one extra layer. This is the first test of depth 13 that is about depth. Within the plateau the evidence points one way -- 10, 11 and 12 are all width 512 and the deepest won -- and this asks whether that trend continues past the rounding boundary that has been hiding it.
proposal.risk:
This is a two-constant edit and someone reading the ledger could reasonably call it two changes. I think that is wrong -- ASPECT_RATIO is not an independent knob here, it is the coefficient in the depth->width formula, and any depth change at constant width must move it -- but the objection is fair enough that I am stating it rather than hiding it. The alternative, changing depth alone, is what t0459 did and it measured something else entirely.
The extra long-window layer is the real confound: if this wins, part of the win may be the fifth full-context layer rather than the extra block, and separating them would need a 13-character window pattern holding the long count at four. If it wins I will run that separation before believing the depth story.

t0469 ended as timeout. Hypothesis: Warm retry for the EXHAUSTIVE autotune search, queued in advance because a timeout was the registered expectation rather than a surprise.

Throughput is the only axis in this campaign still paying, and the control run just priced it properly. t0445 ran the champion model byte-for-byte with compile mode reverted: 2744 steps and 0.962233 against the champion's 2806 and 0.961216.     depth 12: 504 -> model_dim 512, 4 heads   <- champion
    depth 13: 546 -> model_dim 640, 5 heads

It isolates depth at constant width -- the only clean depth measurement available on this axis -- and it also tests something about the champion: depth 12 is the LARGEST depth that still rounds to width 512, so the champion sits exactly at the top of a width plateau. If depth 11 loses, 12 is the best point on that plateau and the axis is genuinely closed at the champion. If depth 11 wins, the plateau's optimum is below 12 and the early depth exploration -- which was really exploring model SIZE, not depth -- missed it.

payload.finding:
t0472 improved the prior champion: val_bpb=0.961036, delta=-0.000180. Hypothesis: Fourth attempt at a question that is still unanswered. Three prior runs were killed by contention -- two guard aborts near 29% MFU, one at 18.1% -- and none said anything about the edit; each had a normally descending loss when killed. Checking the ledger, the only nodes carrying this zero-init that ever produced a score are t0046, t0363 and t0394, and each bundled it with a different change under test, so its own effect has never been measured in 465 trials.

It is also the cheapest bet available: initialisation runs before torch.compile, so the graph is unchanged, the inductor cache hits, max-autotune is retained and the comparison is unhandicapped -- the shortest exposure window of anything I can queue, which matters on a contended box.

The champion's initialiser does not do what its own comment says. The gate-init block reads 'Gate weights init to zero (sigmoid(0)=0.5, scaled by 2 -> 1.0 = neutral)' and then zeroes only ve_gate. attn_gate -- added when the attention output gate was promoted at t0353 -- appears exactly twice in the file, at its definition and its use, and keeps PyTorch's default nn.Linear init.

I measured what that actually does rather than estimating it, and the measurement changed the hypothesis. Feeding rms_norm'd activations through a default-initialised nn.Linear(128, 4) and applying 2*sigmoid gives mean 1.0015, std 0.2628, min 0.155, max 1.828, with the middle 98% spanning 0.425 to 1.575. Crucially the PER-HEAD means are 0.9999, 1.0057, 1.0015 and 0.9990 -- essentially exactly 1.0. So there is no systematic per-head mis-scaling. The scatter is per-token: at initialisation the gate multiplies each head's attention output by input-dependent noise with the right mean and a large spread.

That is a different mechanism from the one I first wrote down. My analytic estimate said 0.72-1.28 and attributed it to relative mis-scaling between neighbouring matrices, by analogy to t0440 and t0443. The real effect is twice as wide and is multiplicative noise, not mis-scaling -- and noise cuts both ways, since it can regularise as easily as it can damage. Zeroing the weight removes it entirely and starts every gate at exactly 1.0, which is what the comment intends.

History still favours testing it: t0046 proposed this gate WITH the zero-init and lost on raw while winning on mechanism; t0353 re-bought the mechanism 300 trials later WITHOUT it and was promoted, so the champion inherited the version missing the line. Three later nodes carried the zeroed form but each bundled it with another change under test, so its own effect is unmeasured.

Initialisation runs before torch.compile and does not change the traced graph, so the inductor cache still hits and there is no wall-clock risk -- unlike every structural probe since t0439, this is an unhandicapped comparison against the champion on equal throughput footing. I should have realised this at t0443, which reverted compile mode for an init-only change and paid 2.2% of steps for nothing.
